text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Protesting farmers are expected to drive to Parliament in 200 tractors this morning to formally present a petition outlining their grievances to Speaker Zoltan Gal.

- At his monthly press briefing, Prime Minister Gyula Horn yesterday conceded that all sections of society have worded mostly legitimate claims, but noted that the government must bear in mind the budget and the results of economic stabilisation.
- Gen. John Seehan, Supreme Commander of NATO for the Atlantic region, met Defence Minister Gyorgy Keleti in Budapest on Monday.
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs conferred with Chilean Foreign Minister Jose Miguel Insulza in Santiago on Monday regarding an investment protection agreement and a pact on avoiding double taxation.

- Parliament Monday began a general debate of a report put together by the so-called "Oilgate" commission after 16 months of investigation into alleged conflicts of interest in arranging oil shipments from Russia made as part payment of debt owed to Hungary, beginning in 1994.
- Former prime minister Peter Boross called on the cabinet to immediately stop the privatisation of the electricity industry and broadcaster Antenna Hungaria.
- The Christian Democratic caucus yesterday gave a vote of confidence to group leader Tamas Isepy.
- The Magyar Kulkereskedelmi Bank signed an agreement yesterday on a DM 150 million syndcated loan from 20 Western European and Japanese banks, an MKB communique reports.
- Two unidentified armed men disguised as policemen stole nearly HUF 10 million from an OTP bank in Budapest's third district on Monday afternoon.

- Five Martfu residents, including three policemen, independently reported seeing an unidentified object plummeting in flames over the eastern plain and exploding noiselessly before landing near the Tisza river on Sunday.
NEPSZABADSAG
- March 15 commemorations are detailed in this paper. State and opposition parties have arranged separate events to mark the occasion.
NAPI GAZDASAG

- The domestic food industry has been renewed in the past six years to a point where 90 percent of food industry companies are privately owned and 60 percent are held by foreign investors, strategic investors or market leading multinationals, said National Association of Food Processors chairman Laszlo Piros.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Twenty parties will be invited to submit bids for a stake in the Kereskedelmi es Hitelbank Rt., according to a strategy drawn up for the bank's privatisation.

- Raffeisen Unicbank appointed former National Bank of Hungary president Ferenc Bartha as chairman of the board of directors at its annual general meeting yesterday. The shareholders also raised the bank's equity by HUF 769 million via a share issue.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Share prices saw a sharp drop at the Budapest Stock Exchange on Monday after a steep 13-month-long rise and stagnation in February.
- Trading in shares of the brokerage house Quaestor begins on the Budapest Stock Exchange today.
